issue.title: Can't see where I am when I use Tab
body: I use a keyboard instead of a mouse. On the homepage, when I press Tab, there's no outline at all, so I can't tell which link or button I'm on.
I tried to sign up to volunteer for Friday, pressed Enter on what I guessed was the right button, and ended up somewhere else. Could you bring back the focus indicator?

task.instruction: Select "Move focus into the page", then use Tab and Shift+Tab to reach the Volunteer button and press Enter.
task.afterReproduce: You found it, but could you see which element had focus along the way? Now fix the stylesheet.

options.label: Keep the rule and add a hover outline instead
options.feedback: Hover only responds to a mouse pointer. Keyboard users still get no indicator.

options.label: Use a subtle light gray outline so it doesn't affect the design
options.feedback: There is an outline now, but at 1px and barely above 1:1 contrast against white, most people won't see it. Aim for at least 2px and 3:1.

options.label: Replace it with a clear :focus-visible outline
options.feedback: Clear 3px outline with strong contrast. :focus-visible shows it for keyboard users without changing what mouse users see.

merged.reply: That did it. I can see exactly where I am now, and I'm signed up for Friday. Thank you!
learn: Never remove the focus outline without replacing it.
Use :focus-visible to show a strong indicator to keyboard users.
Focus indicators need visible size and at least 3:1 contrast.
